chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Faddal from one who informed him from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prays and a woman is beside him or to his side, he said: 'If her prostration is with his bowing, there is no harm.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is a man's prayer valid if a woman is praying beside him?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the spatial dynamics of prayer, specifically addressing the concern of visual distraction (*fitnah*) between genders. The ruling establishes that if the woman's prostration aligns temporally with the man's bowing, the visual field is sufficiently occupied or minimized, rendering the man's prayer valid without objection. This highlights the Shia juristic focus on practical conditions of modesty and concentration rather than rigid, absolute separation during congregational or family prayers.
